page: Microsoft Azure E4-2s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with constrained vCPU sizing. Based on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor operating at 4.2 GHz. The instance allocates two dedicated virtual CPUs backed by a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled. It features 32.0 GB of system memory, providing a high ratio of 16.0 GB per vCPU. Cache resources include 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and access to a large 260 MB L3 cache pool. The underlying host platform runs on Microsoft Hyper-V.

Hardware accelerator and storage profiles reflect specialized provisioning. The instance includes no discrete graphics processing units and comes with no local storage disks bundled, relying instead on network-attached remote block storage via Azure Premium Storage capabilities. Additionally, the instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. The instruction set includes AVX-512 vector extensions along with Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX tile and int8), alongside AES and SHA cryptographic accelerations.

Benchmark outcomes demonstrate a split between strong single-threaded execution and constrained parallel capacity. Single-core performance is robust, reflected in a Geekbench single-core score of 2146.0 and single-threaded gzip compression achieving 31.19 GB/sec. However, because the instance provides only one physical core across two threads, multi-threaded output is limited, scoring 2638.0 on Geekbench multi-core and 1992.69 on stress-ng multi-core tests. Measured uncached memory bandwidth registers at 21.51 GB/sec read and 14.37 GB/sec write. In-memory data store testing demonstrates 2.85 million Redis SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput measures 4.56 GB/sec.

The qualitative profile of the E4-2s_v6 centers on cost efficiency for memory-demanding workloads with software licensing structures tied to core counts. By offering 32.0 GB of memory across just two vCPUs, it prevents overpaying for unnecessary processor licenses while sustaining substantial in-memory capacity. The primary tradeoff is raw compute parallelism, making this instance suitable for memory-heavy databases, caching layers, low-concurrency data services, and enterprise middleware rather than computationally dense batch processing.

The instance contains no bundled local storage and zero GPUs, relying on remote block storage solutions. Benchmark assessments reveal strong single-core performance, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 2146.0 and rapid single-threaded gzip compression. The instance provides a cost-efficient architecture for software environments constrained by per-core licensing fees, making it suitable for memory-intensive caching tiers, enterprise middleware, and small relational or in-memory databases requiring significant memory footprint without extensive CPU throughput.
